summary: Keeping, breeding, and selling a roof rat is legal in Missouri with no state permit. The Wildlife Code expressly lets non-native mammals be 'bought, sold, possessed, transported, and exhibited without permit' (3 CSR 10-9.110), and the prohibited-species list (3 CSR 10-4.117) names other rodents (genus Mastomys) but NOT Rattus. It's not a 'dangerous wild animal' (RSMo 578.023 = large carnivores/reptiles), and the Animal Care Facilities Act licensing applies only to dogs/cats. The one requirement: importing a pet rodent needs a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (rodents = 'miscellaneous animals'). Check your city/county ordinance, and never release one.

keep.why: Under 3 CSR 10-9.110, non-native mammals may be possessed without a Wildlife Code permit, except federally endangered species or those on the prohibited-species (3 CSR 10-4.117) / Class II (3 CSR 10-9.240) lists. R. rattus is non-native and on none of those (the prohibited list names genus Mastomys, not Rattus), and it's not a 'dangerous wild animal' under RSMo 578.023. No permit to keep one.

breed.why: The 3 CSR 10-9.110 non-native exemption covers propagation too, and the Animal Care Facilities Act (RSMo 273.325) defines 'animal' as dogs/cats only — so no state breeder license reaches pet rats. General cruelty/care law still applies.

sell_give.why: 3 CSR 10-9.110 expressly allows non-native mammals to be 'bought, sold... without permit,' and the ACFA pet-shop/dealer licensing turns on the dog/cat definition (RSMo 273.325), so selling or giving away pet rats triggers no state license.

transport.why: Within Missouri, no Wildlife Code permit is needed (3 CSR 10-9.110). For IMPORT, the Dept of Agriculture (2 CSR 30-2.010) requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection within 30 days for animals entering Missouri; rodents are 'miscellaneous animals,' so a pet rat should travel with a CVI. The Wildlife Code's no-release rule (3 CSR 10-4.110) bars ever liberating one.

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rodent into Missouri requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (2 CSR 30-2.010; rodents = 'miscellaneous animals'). No CVI for in-state movement.
restrictions.where_to_file: Missouri Dept of Agriculture, Animal Health Division

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat (3 CSR 10-4.110). Local city/county ordinances (e.g., Kansas City, St. Louis) may add limits — check yours.
